hook_text: 5 packets of 23 sweets. No calculator. Split the 23 and you are done in four seconds.
clip_script: Five packets, 23 sweets each. 5 times 23 feels hard. Split the 23 into 20 and 3. 5 times 20 is 100. 5 times 3 is 15. Together, 115. That is the distributive property: split, multiply each part, add. Now the minibus: 4 rows of 3 seats, or 3 columns of 4. Same 12 seats. Swap the order for plus and times whenever it helps. 7 plus 58? Start at 58. Three numbers? Group the easy pair first: 7 plus 8 plus 2, do 8 plus 2, that is 10, then 17. One warning: never swap a minus or a divide. 10 minus 4 is 6, 4 minus 10 is not. And zero? 348 plus 0 is still 348. Adding nothing does nothing. Swap, group, split. Three freedoms that make every sum easier.
visual_style: Whiteboard packet of 23 splitting into 20 and 3 with the 5 jumping to each; a minibus seat grid rotating; pairs of numbers sliding together into tens.
pacing: The split trick first, then swap and group in quick examples, then the one warning and zero.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find a split that makes your hardest times table easy.
